newsitem.title: USA: Integra treatment to be used in U.K. cases.
newsitem.headline: Integra treatment to be used in U.K. cases.

text.p: Integra LifeSciences Corp on Wednesday said it received an "exceptional circumstances" approval from the British Department of Health for use of INTEGRA Artificial Skin in two cases involving badly scarred children.

The current indication in Britain is primarily for patients with severe, life-threatening burns, the company said. The special-use approval for the product, which promotes the growth of a new, permanent dermis, was granted on humanitarian grounds, Integra said.

The first patient to receive INTEGRA in reconstructive surgery is a five-year-old girl who was the victim of child abuse, Integra said. The second is that of a 16-month-old girl who has a large pigmented birthmark on her left lower leg. The condition can carry the risk of malignancy in the future.
INTEGRA Artificial Skin received pre-marketing approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in March 1996.
